([[Pennsauken Township, New Jersey]]) | college = * [[Arizona Western Matadors|Arizona Western]] (2020–2023) * [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB]] (2023–2025) * [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2026]]) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2026]]) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] (2026) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2026) * Big Ten All-Defensive Team (2026) * 2× First-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2024, 2025) * 2× AAC Defensive Player of the Year (2024, 2025) * [[American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] MVP (2024) * Second-team [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] All-American (2023) * Third-team NJCAA All-American (2022) }} '''Yaxel Okari Lendeborg''' (born September 30, 2002) is an American-Dominican [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Western Matadors]], [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|UAB Blazers]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He was an [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA national champion]], [[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans#2026 Consensus All-America team|consensus All-American]] and the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] with Michigan in 2026. ==Early life== Lendeborg was born on September 30, 2002.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Yaxel-Lendeborg/Summary/177627|publisher=[[RealGM]]|title=Yaxel Lendeborg}} He was born in [[Puerto Rico]] and his family moved to [[Ohio]] when he was age two.{{Cite web|url=https://kyma.com/news/special-reports/2023/05/17/from-the-house-to-d1-the-story-of-arizona-westerns-yaxel-lendeborg/|publisher=[[KYMA-DT]]|title=From the House to D1, the story of Arizona Western's Yaxel Lendeborg|date=May 17, 2023|author=Lopez, Luis}} He is of [[People of the Dominican Republic|Dominican]] descent, with both his parents having been top basketball players in the country.{{Cite web|url=https://record.acento.com.do/baloncesto/yaxel-lendeborg-la-nueva-promesa-del-baloncesto-dominicano-24184.html|website=record.acento.com.do|language=Spanish|title=Yaxel Lendeborg: La nueva promesa del baloncesto dominicano|trans-title=Yaxel Lendeborg: The new promise of Dominican basketball|date=August 10, 2022|author=Sulbaran, Maykell}} He later moved with his family to [[Pennsauken Township, New Jersey]], when he was eight.{{Cite news|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2022/08/04/memphis-basketball-recruiting-yaxel-lendeborg-arizona-western-college/10188309002/|newspaper=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|via=[[archive.ph]]|title=Meet Yaxel Lendeborg, the Memphis basketball recruit who played just 11 varsity games|date=August 4, 2022|author=Munz, Jason|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250201001207/https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2022/08/04/memphis-basketball-recruiting-yaxel-lendeborg-arizona-western-college/10188309002/|archive-date=2025-02-01}} He attended [[Pennsauken High School]] and tried out for the [[basketball]] team; he made the squad as a [[freshman]], but was cut from the team mid-season due to poor academic performance. Lendeborg later missed the next two seasons due to poor grades as well. As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], he entered a dual-enrollment program with [[Camden County College]] and his grades improved enough that he was able to join the Pennsauken varsity basketball team with 11 games left in the season. In 11 games played, he helped Pennsauken compile a record of 10–1.{{Cite web|url=https://awcmatadors.com/sports/mbkb/2022-23/bios/lendeborg_yaxel_u5qd|publisher=[[Arizona Western Matadors]]|title=Yaxel Lendeborg}} He signed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Western Matadors]]. ==College career== ===Arizona Western=== As a freshman at Arizona Western in 2020–21, Lendeborg played in a [[COVID-19]] shortened season and averaged 6.1 points and 7.1 rebounds in 14 games. The following season, he appeared in 31 games and averaged 12.0 points and 11.0 rebounds per game, leading his conference in rebounds and was named a third-team [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) [[All-American]], first-team all-region, the [[Arizona Community College Athletic Conference]] (ACCAC) Player of the Year and the ACCAC Freshman of the Year. In the 2022–23 season with the Matadors, he was named a second-team All-American, first-team all-region and the ACCAC Player of the Year. Lendeborg averaged 17.2 points and an NJCAA-leading 13.0 rebounds per game in his final season.{{Cite web|url=https://kyma.com/sports/college-sports/2022/11/15/lendeborg-to-hit-the-bright-lights-of-new-york-signs-with-st-johns/|publisher=[[KYMA-DT]]|title=Lendeborg to hit the bright lights of New York, signs with St. John's|last1=Johnson|first1=Cole|last2=Gross|first2=Scott|date=November 16, 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/news/2023/5/1/mens-basketball-two-time-juco-all-american-yaxel-lendeborg-signs-with-uab-mbb|publisher=[[UAB Blazers]]|title=Two-Time JUCO All-American Yaxel Lendeborg Signs with UAB MBB|date=May 1, 2023}} He finished his tenure at Arizona Western as the NJCAA's all-time leading rebounder with 429 total. After finishing his career at Arizona Western, Lendeborg signed his [[national letter of intent]] to play for the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]] in November 2022. However, he was not retained after the hiring of new head coach [[Rick Pitino]] in 2023. ===UAB=== On April 29, 2023, Lendeborg transferred to the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]] (UAB) to play for the [[UAB Blazers men's basketball|Blazers]] following his career at Arizona Western.{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/uab/2024/01/right-shots-right-time-yaxel-lendeborgs-expanded-abilities-yielding-high-return-for-uab-basketball.html|website=[[AL.com]]|title='Right shots, right time': Yaxel Lendeborg's expanded abilities yielding high return for UAB basketball|author=Dudley, Evan|date=January 19, 2024}}{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/article/yaxel-lendeborg-uab-st-johns--209204139/|publisher=[[247Sports]]|title=Former St. John's commit Yaxel Lendeborg signs with UAB|date=April 29, 2023|author=London, DuShawn}} On November 25, 2023, in the sixth game of the season he recorded his first career NCAA double-double against [[2023–24 Furman Paladins men's basketball team|Furman]]; scoring 19 points, ten rebounds and adding five blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/yaxel-lendeborg-1/gamelog/ |title=Yaxel Lendeborg Career Game Log |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=May 31, 2025}} On January 2, 2024, Lendeborg had 23 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high seven blocked shots against [[2023–24 UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball team|UTSA]]. On February 8, he scored 17 points and had a career-high 21 rebounds against [[2023–24 Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball team|Florida Atlantic]] and his future head coach [[Dusty May]]. In total during the 2023–24 season, he played in 35 games and averaged 13.8 points, 10.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.1 blocks per game, earning the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Defensive Player of the Year, the [[2024 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|2024 AAC tournament]] [[Most valuable player|MVP]] and first-team All-AAC honors.{{Cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/yaxel-lendeborg/10723|publisher=[[UAB Blazers]]|title=Yaxel Lendeborg}} Lendeborg returned to UAB for a second season in [[2024–25 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|2024-25]].{{Cite web |author=Dudley, Evan |date=March 27, 2024 |title=UAB basketball's Yaxel Lendeborg {{as written|annou|ces [sic]}} return to Blazers for 2024-2025 season |url=https://www.al.com/uab/2024/03/uab-basketballs-yaxel-lendeborg-annouces-return-to-blazers-for-2024-2025-season.html |website=[[AL.com]]}} On March 14, 2025, he scored 30 points, 20 rebounds, eight assists, five steals and four blocked shots against [[2024–25 East Carolina Pirates men's basketball team|East Carolina]] in the [[2025 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|2025 AAC tournament]]. The points, assists and steals were each career-highs. In 2024-25, Lendeborg repeated as an All-AAC first-team selection, and the AAC Defensive Player of the Year. He became the fifth player in UAB Blazers history to score 1,000 points in a span of two seasons.{{cite web|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2025/3/11/american-athletic-conference-announces-2024-25-mens-basketball-awards.aspx |title=American Athletic Conference Announces 2024-25 Men's Basketball Awards |date=2 April 2025 }} Lendeborg started all 37 games for the Blazers, averaging 17.7 points, 11.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.7 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/sidearm.nextgen.sites/uabsports.com/stats/mbball/2024/pdf/cume.pdf?t=1743091324464 |title=2024-25 UAB Men's Basketball Overall Statistics |date=March 26, 2025}} He became one of only two players in NCAA division one history to record over 600 points, 400 rebounds and 150 assists in a single season, joining legend [[Larry Bird]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44544277/uab-star-big-man-yaxel-lendeborg-commits-michigan |title=UAB star big man Yaxel Lendeborg commits to Michigan |website=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Jonathan |last=Givony |date=April 5, 2025 |access-date=April 5, 2025}} In addition, Lendeborg led the NCAA with 26 double-doubles and recorded a program single-season record of 420 total rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/556 |title=Men's Basketball NCAA Division I Double Doubles (2024-25) |website=[[NCAA]] |date=April 1, 2025 |access-date=April 5, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/news/2025/3/26/mens-basketball-uab-falls-in-ot-at-uc-irvine |title=UAB Falls in OT at UC Irvine|website=UAB Athletics |date=March 26, 2025}} Lendeborg also holds the program record with 45 career double-doubles, was the 25th member of the 1,000-point club (1,136), fifth in rebounds (790) and fourth in blocked shots (138).{{Cite web |title=Yaxel Lendeborg - Men's Basketball |url=https://uabsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/yaxel-lendeborg/10723 |access-date=2025-03-27 |website=UAB Athletics |language=en}} Following the season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]] and was the No. 1 ranked player in the portal according to [[247Sports]], [[CBS Sports]] and [[On3.com]], while ''[[The Athletic]]'' ranked him 2nd and [[ESPN]] ranked him third.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/longformarticle/ranking-the-top-50-players-in-the-college-basketball-transfer-portal-248138031 |title=Ranking the top 50 players in the college basketball transfer portal |website=[[247Sports]] |first=Isaac |last=Trotter |date=April 2, 2025 |access-date=April 5, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/04/top-player-in-transfer-portal-commits-to-michigan.html|title=Top player in transfer portal commits to Michigan|website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=April 5, 2025 |access-date=November 28, 2025}} ===Michigan=== On April 5, 2025, Lendeborg transferred to the [[University of Michigan]] to play for [[Dusty May]] and the [[2025–26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Wolverines]]. He also entered the [[2025 NBA draft]] process in addition to transferring. On May 27, he withdrew from the NBA draft and chose to play his final season of college basketball in [[Ann Arbor]].{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2025/05/27/uab-transfer-yaxel-lendeborg-to-withdraw-from-nba-draft-play-for-michigan-wolverines-basketball/83877398007/ |title=UAB transfer Yaxel Lendeborg to withdraw from NBA Draft, play for Michigan next season |website=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=May 27, 2025 |access-date=May 27, 2025}} Lendeborg was projected to be a late first round or early second round selection in the draft, with the potential to earn $2.7 million in the first year and $14 million total in a four-year rookie contract if selected in the late first round. It was believed that Michigan offered around $3 million in guaranteed [[Name, image and likeness]] compensation to sway him.{{cite web|url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/2025/5/12/24426072/yaxel-lendeborg-nba-draft-michigan-basketball-nil-dusty-may|title=How much NIL money would it take for Yaxel Lendeborg to stay at Michigan?|access-date=November 28, 2025|date=May 12, 2025|author=Voss, Kellen|publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/2025/5/27/24438025/yaxel-lendeborg-michigan-basketball-nba-draft-dusty-may-nil-danny-wolf-vlad-goldin|title=3 thoughts on Yaxel Lendeborg choosing Michigan over the NBA Draft|access-date=November 28, 2025|date=May 27, 2025|author=Voss, Kellen|publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2025/05/15/nba-draft-2025-combine-nil-money-yaxel-landeborg/83650225007/|title=NIL is giving college basketball players the power. Should the NBA draft wait?|access-date=November 28, 2025|date=May 15, 2025|author=Giannotto, Mark|work=[[USA Today]]}} It is believed that Michigan gave Lendeborg about $5 million between NIL and revenue share and that this was less than the $7–9 million deal [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] had offered him.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/yaxel-lendeborg-nil-michigan-salary-not-match-kentucky-offer/|title=Michigan star Yaxel Lendeborg turned down $7M-$9M Kentucky offer to play for Dusty May|access-date=March 18, 2026|date=March 17, 2026|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Salerno, Cameron}} Lendeborg was named a preseason first-team All-American by the [[Associated Press]], [[Blue Ribbon College Basketball Yearbook|Blue Ribbon Yearbook]], [[ESPN]], and [[SB Nation]]; as well as a second-team selection by [[CBS Sports]], ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', ''[[The Sporting News]]'' and ''[[USA Today]]''.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/10/27/2025-26-michigan-mens-basketball-awards-and-honors |title=Awards and Honors: Lendeborg Named to Sporting News Preseason All-America Second Team|website=University of Michigan Athletics|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|date=November 10, 2025|access-date=November 11, 2025}}{{cite web |author=Sweeney, Kevin|title=Sports Illustrated’s 2025–26 College Basketball Preseason All-Americans|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2025/10/29/college-basketball-all-america-team-preseason/86951196007/|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 29, 2025 |access-date=November 10, 2025}}{{cite web |author=Rutherford, Mike|title=Meet our college basketball preseason All-America teams for men’s 2025-26 season|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/1087601/meet-our-college-basketball-preseason-all-america-teams-for-mens-2025-26-season|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 28, 2025 |access-date=November 10, 2025}} He was [[Joe Lunardi]] and SB Nation’s preseason National Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/michigan-mens-basketball/96286/michigan-basketball-joe-lunardi-predictions-yaxel-lendeborg-national-championship-dusty-may|title=Joe Lunardi predicts Michigan Basketball to win National Championship|access-date=November 10, 2025|date=October 30, 2025|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|author=Singer, Jacob}} He was also named to the preseason [[Naismith College Player of the Year]], [[NABC Player of the Year]], and [[Karl Malone Award]] watchlists. On November 3 against [[2025–26 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]], Lendeborg was limited in his debut with a right hand injury. He came off the bench and recorded twelve points (100% shooting: 4 FG, 2 FT), four rebounds, and three assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/11/michigan-basketball-injuries-2-miss-opener-yaxel-lendeborg-limited.html |title=Michigan basketball injuries: 2 miss opener, Yaxel Lendeborg limited |website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=November 4, 2025 |access-date=November 11, 2025}} In late November, he led the Wolverines to a championship in the [[2025 Players Era Festival]], defeating [[2025–26 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]] by 40 points, No. 21 [[2025–26 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] by 30 points and No. 12 [[2025–26 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] by 40 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401831214 |title=No. 7 Michigan dominates No. 12 Gonzaga 101-61 to win Players Era Championship |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 27, 2025 |access-date=November 27, 2025}} Lendeborg was named the Players Era Championship MVP after averaging 17.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.3 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/college-basketball-ap-player-of-week-6866f2595b9da58550e2572bb7fe4fef |title=Michigan's Yaxel Lendeborg is the AP men's college basketball player of the week |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 2, 2025 |access-date=December 2, 2025}} He was also named as the week four [[Big Ten Conference]] Player of the Week and the [[Associated Press]] National Player of the Week.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/59030/ |title=Michigan and Penn State Score Men's Basketball Weekly Honors |website=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=December 1, 2025 |access-date=December 1, 2025}} On December 13 against [[2025–26 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], Lendeborg had a season-high 29 points, career-high nine assists, eight rebounds, three blocks and two steals.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/12/13/mens-basketball-lendeborg-leads-way-as-michigan-stays-perfect-with-win-at-maryland |title=Lendeborg Leads Way as Michigan Stays Perfect With Win at Maryland |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=December 13, 2025 |access-date=December 13, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401825408 |title=Yaxel Lendeborg scores 29 points and No. 2 Michigan stays unbeaten with 101-83 win over Maryland |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 13, 2025 |access-date=December 13, 2025}} Lendeborg was named on the January 25-person [[Wooden Award]] midseason watchlist.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/page/menswoodenaward01072026/aj-dybantsa-cameron-boozer-freshmen-mens-wooden-award-midseason-top-25-list-2026|title=AJ Dybantsa, more freshmen headline men's Wooden Award midseason top 25|access-date=February 21, 2026|date=January 7, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Borzello, Jeff}} On January 30, 2026, Michigan defeated No. 7 [[2025–26 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in their [[Michigan–Michigan State men's basketball rivalry|in-state rivalry]] game, 83–71, behind 26 points and 12 rebounds from Lendeborg; his fourth double-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401825481 |title=No. 3 Michigan beats No. 7 Michigan State 83-71, takes sole possession of 1st place in Big Ten |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=January 30, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/1/30/mens-basketball-wolverines-stifle-second-half-spartan-comeback-to-win-battle-at-breslin |title=Wolverines Stifle Second-Half Spartan Comeback to Win Battle at Breslin |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=January 30, 2026 |access-date=January 30, 2026}} On February 8, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] 82–61 in the [[Michigan–Ohio State men's basketball rivalry|rivalry]] rematch. Lendeborg posted 14 points and a season-high 14 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-basketball/aday-mara-scores-24-points-no-2-michigan-routs-rival-ohio-state-82-61|title=Aday Mara Scores 24 Points as No. 2 Michigan Routs Rival Ohio State, 82-61|access-date=February 9, 2026|date=February 8, 2026|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2026/02/09/michigan-basketball-team-building-ohio-state/88581062007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z11xx13p119550c119550v11xx13d--xx--b--xx--&gca-ft=224&gca-ds=sophi|title=Michigan basketball finds another level after team-building exercise|access-date=February 9, 2026|date=February 9, 2026|author=Garcia, Tony|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}} Lendeborg was named on the February 20-person Wooden late midseason watchlist, which clarified that the official final ballot would be a 15-man list.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/page/menswoodenaward02102026/mens-college-basketball-2026-wooden-award-late-midseason-top-20-short-list|title=Cameron Boozer headlines freshman-heavy men's Wooden Award top 20|access-date=February 21, 2026|date=February 10, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Borzello, Jeff}} On March 8, Lendeborg scored 27 points in a win against No. 8 Michigan State. Michigan finished as the Big Ten regular season champions and with an all-time conference record for wins, 19–1. In his two games versus the Spartans he scored 53 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401825568|title=Yaxel Lendeborg scores 27, No. 3 Michigan beats No. 8 Michigan State 90-80 to sweep season series|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 8, 2026}} Following the regular season, he was named [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big Ten Player of the Year]] by both the coaches and media; Michigan's first player of the year honoree since [[Nik Stauskas]] in 2014. Lendeborg was also first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] by the coaches and media, the conference's only unanimous first-team selection by the latter, and joined his teammates, [[Morez Johnson Jr.]] and [[Aday Mara]], on the Big Ten All-Defensive Team.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/10/mens-basketball-lendeborg-earns-big-ten-player-of-the-year-as-u-m-hauls-15-all-conference-honors|title=Lendeborg Earns Big Ten Player of the Year as U-M Hauls 15 All-Conference Honors|date=March 10, 2026|access-date=March 10, 2026|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|publisher=University of Michigan Athletics}}{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/59585/|title=Big Ten Announces 2026 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors|date=March 10, 2026|access-date=March 11, 2026|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} Nationally, Lendeborg was selected as a [[2026 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans#2026 Consensus All-America team|consensus first-team All-American]] by the four major selectors: Associated Press, [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]], ''The Sporting News'', and the [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]].
